exploit_name: Unsigned validity window metadata allows relayer to alter signature expiration
description: The signature validation mechanism extracts validUntil and validAfter timestamps from the trailing 12 bytes of the user operation signature, but these values are never cryptographically bound to the signed message. A relayer can alter the validity window while preserving the ECDSA signature's validity, effectively removing intended time-based restrictions.
attack_scenario: Attacker observes a signed user operation with a short validity window. Attacker strips or modifies the appended validUntil/validAfter bytes. Since these bytes are not included in the signed hash, the ECDSA signature remains valid. Attacker submits the modified operation after the intended expiry.
root_cause: The signature validation mechanism extracts validUntil and validAfter timestamps from the trailing 12 bytes of the user operation signature, but these values are never cryptographically bound to the signed message. A relayer can alter the validity window while preserving the ECDSA signature's validity, effectively removing intended time-based restrictions.
fix_description: Include validUntil and validAfter in the signed hash computation before applying the EIP-191 prefix. Conditionally incorporate metadata values when a 77-byte signature is present.
notes: An attacker observing a signed user operation can extend or remove its validity window and resubmit it later, even if the signer intended it to expire quickly. This enables execution outside the signer's intended timeframe, potentially causing unwanted transfers.
